note: Lab H72 (2026-10-13), round 1 long video, NEW FORMAT: a quiz people search for. 'English Vocabulary Quiz B1', 20 questions with our synonym spin: each question names a plain word or phrase and asks for the better word in a sentence, three choices with letters, a 5-second countdown with ticks, then the answer in the sentence and one more example. Four rounds of five (chapters), a score card, a held closing card for the end screen. The search phrase is the first thing said and shown. Words from our best-clicked old videos (happy, excited, sad, interesting, beautiful, nice, strong, stupid, help, change, love, ensure, provide, develop/get better, effective, also, but, because). Revised after the review by both expert sources (2026-10-13): no title card - question 1 is on screen at 0:00 and the rules are said over it; an emoji picture on every question card; the closing card names the next video (Stop Saying "Very": 30 words, aXghTlqKcHQ).

card.headline: Question 1 of 20
card.sub: Find a better word for "very happy"
card.question: I was ___ when I passed the exam.
card.answer: I was delighted when I passed the exam.
card.note: "We are delighted with our new home."

beats.speech: English vocabulary quiz, B1 level: twenty questions, five seconds each. Question one. Find a better word for very happy. I was, blank, when I passed the exam. Delighted, disappointed, or confused? | Delighted. I was delighted when I passed the exam. One more example: We are delighted with our new home. That's one point if you got it. Keep counting.
